## TL;DR

Added `just deploy-phone` — a Bun TypeScript port of the Laisen/Tiao Tailscale adb deploy flow for RepoOS Hub. Debug builds use `applicationIdSuffix ".dev"` (`org.repoos.mobile.dev`) so they install beside release. Phone targets come from env or `~/.config/repoos-hub/phone` with no default IP in the repo. Vitest covers connect, scan fallback, launch-component validation, signature mismatch, and `--no-build` / `--no-scan`. No real install was run; Nick should approve the first live deploy.

## Work and rationale

I read the Laisen reference on the thinkpad (`deploy-phone.sh`, `launch-component.sh`, `phone-deploy.md`) and matched its behaviour: resolve target from `REPOOS_HUB_PHONE`, then `REPOOS_HUB_PHONE_PORT` + saved IP, then the config file; try saved address, other open adb serials for the same IP, then scan TCP 30000–49999 (nmap when available, otherwise socket probes); wait one second after `adb connect` before requiring `get-state device`; persist the last working `ip:port`; on `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` print one-time `adb uninstall org.repoos.mobile.dev` guidance.

Unlike Laisen, this repo must not ship a default phone IP. When nothing is configured, the script fails early with a clear message instead of guessing an address.

The implementation splits `scripts/lib/launch-component.ts`, `scripts/lib/hub-phone-deploy.ts` (testable core + injectable adb runner), and `scripts/deploy-phone.ts` (CLI). The justfile mobile group wires `deploy-phone *FLAGS` to `bun scripts/deploy-phone.ts`. The build step calls `just build-android` so web shell sync stays aligned with the native build, not gradle alone.

## Approaches tried

The Laisen bash script was the behavioural spec; Tiao's copy confirmed the same structure with different env var names. I chose TypeScript + dependency injection for tests rather than a bash harness with fake adb on PATH, because AGENTS.md requires Bun scripts and the main vitest gate already lives under `src/ui-app/tests/`.

Gradle `debug { applicationIdSuffix ".dev" }` mirrors Laisen's side-by-side dev install. Release `applicationId` stays `org.repoos.mobile`. Debug `app/src/debug/res/values/strings.xml` sets the launcher label **RepoOS Hub Dev** without touching release strings. Launch uses fully qualified `org.repoos.mobile.dev/org.repoos.mobile.MainActivity` — never `.MainActivity`, which would resolve against the suffixed id.

## Challenges and blockers

Port-scan tests needed careful fake-adb sequencing: the saved port must fail connect while a scanned port succeeds only after connect, without accidentally marking the stale port as ready. The unreachable-phone test had to align `homeDir` and `repoRoot` temp paths so the failure message matched `phoneConfigPath(homeDir)`.

Human verification is still required: this task deliberately does not run `adb install` against Nick's phone. The first real `just deploy-phone` will install **org.repoos.mobile.dev** next to any existing **org.repoos.mobile** release build (or replace an older dev build with the same id).

## Key learnings

Hub deploy reuses the same Tailscale + Wireless debugging ergonomics as Laisen but with stricter privacy: config lives only on the machine (`REPOOS_HUB_*` and `~/.config/repoos-hub/phone`). Documenting the Tailscale warning-triangle toggle and single-session Wireless debugging limit in `docs/phone-deploy.md` should save future port-hunt time.
